CHIEF COMPLAINT
Kidney stone with left flank pain.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Patient is a female presenting with left flank pain that began three days ago. Pain is constant and radiating downward into the lower left flank/groin area. She reports being unable to get comfortable and has not yet passed the stone. This morning she noticed blood in her urine. She denies fever but reports some chills and nausea. She is unable to eat due to pain severity. She reports taking acetaminophen and ibuprofen with minimal relief. This is her third episode of kidney stones; her previous episodes resolved within three to four days. She is currently on day three of symptoms.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Denies fever. Reports chills, nausea, and constant severe pain in left flank. Able to urinate with hematuria noted this morning. Denies chest pain and abdominal pain (pain is localized to flank/back and radiating to groin).

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Hypertension
Diabetes mellitus type 2
Recurrent kidney stones (third episode)
Grade 2/6 systolic ejection murmur (known)

MEDICATIONS
Norvasc 2.5 mg daily for hypertension
Metformin 500 mg daily for diabetes
Acetaminophen as needed
Ibuprofen as needed

ALLERGIES
Not documented

FAMILY HISTORY
Not documented

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient reports enjoying french fries and high-sodium foods; has difficulty with dietary salt restriction.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital signs: Blood pressure elevated at time of visit (likely secondary to pain). Heart: Grade 2/6 systolic ejection murmur appreciated. Lungs: Clear bilaterally, no crackles or wheezes. Abdomen: Tenderness to palpation, no rebound or guarding. Back/Flank: CVA tenderness on right flank, left flank tenderness consistent with kidney stone with inflammation.

RESULTS
Recent A1C: 7.3 (elevated). Home blood glucose readings: low 100s. Prior glucose level two months ago: approximately 300. Home blood pressure readings: systolic 130-150, diastolic 70-80.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Kidney stone, left side, likely passing. Continue pain management with oxycodone 5 mg every 6-8 hours as needed and acetaminophen for breakthrough pain. Increase fluid intake to promote stone passage. Provide urine strainer to patient to collect passed stone. Refer to urology for evaluation and management of recurrent kidney stones. Continue Norvasc 2.5 mg for hypertension. Continue Metformin 500 mg for diabetes. Refer to dietitian/nutrition for dietary counseling and salt restriction (goal <2300 mg daily). Patient to take home blood pressure readings at least 3 times weekly. Follow up with urology as recommended.
